messages:
ashley.cs: quick escalation — customer (org: coastal-analytics) reports OAuth login via GitHub returns an immediate "state mismatch" and they can't complete auth. They say it worked earlier today but started failing ~10:40 UTC. stack: webapp behind Fastly CDN -> nginx reverse proxy -> our auth callback endpoint. They pasted the error seen in browser:

ashley.cs: Error: "OAuth callback failed: state mismatch (403)". No 500s in our logs.

sara.support: thanks — can you paste the full callback URL the user gets redirected to (the browser address bar) and the registered callback URL in their GitHub app? also any recent deploys?

ashley.cs: user-provided callback (copied from address bar):
```
https://app.coastal-analytics.com/api/auth/callback/github?code=gho_abc123&state=ZjYzYzIzLWV4YW1wbGUtc3RhdGU%3D
```
registered GitHub OAuth app callback: `https://app.coastal-analytics.com/api/auth/callback/github`

ashley.cs: recent deploy? they said no on their side. our deploy-bot shows a Redwood auth runtime deploy 1832456700 ~5m before report. deploy-bot: "auth-service v2.14.1 rolled to prod (canary 100%)"

sara.support: ok ta. two quick checks: 1) is the state param being modified/decoded by CDN/proxy? 2) is there an extra trailing slash or query normalization? can you also check our auth-service request logs for the incoming querystring at 10:40-10:45 UTC.

ashley.cs: grabbed our nginx access log (redacted):
```
10.0.12.45 - - [15/Mar/2026:10:41:02 +0000] "GET /api/auth/callback/github?code=gho_abc123&state=ZjYzYzIzLWV4YW1wbGUtc3RhdGU%3D HTTP/1.1" 302 - "-" "Mozilla/5.0"
```
and our Fastly edge logs show rewrite rules triggered on ?state param at the same time (we have a rule to strip tracking params).

liam.sso: pinged — this smells like state param being normalized/decoded then re-encoded differently, PKCE/state compare fails. also, our latest auth runtime 2.14.1 changed URL canonicalization: we started parsing query string with strict decoding per RFC and we now reject duplicated state params. earlier versions tolerated decoding differences. see changelog note: "normalize query param percent-encoding before state compare".

mike.runtime: adding that our previous canary flagged some edge cases where edge proxies were double-encoding state. Fastly normalizes URLs and our runtime does `decodeURIComponent` once, so if Fastly already decoded a percent-encoded value, we end up comparing different values.

ashley.cs: customer confirms they have a Fastly rule that strips utm_* params and also normalizes querystring ordering. their edge config shows `normalise_querystring` enabled which "decodes and re-encodes".

liam.sso: root cause hypothesis: Fastly normalizer decodes the state token (base64-like string), then our auth runtime decodes again or expects raw encoded string — mismatch occurs. two remediation paths: A) have customer disable the querystring normalizer for /api/auth/callback/github route, or B) make our runtime perform a robust comparison by decoding both sides and comparing canonical bytes.

sara.support: what's lower friction for customer?

liam.sso: fastest is customer toggle on their edge (disable normalization) — immediate unblock. medium term we should patch runtime to canonicalize percent-encoding and compare in decoded form. i'll open a quick fix issue.

mike.runtime: also flagging that recent deploy-bot rollout (v2.14.1) introduced the stricter parsing; rollback is possible but not ideal. can we ship a runtime patch that tolerates decoded inputs within a day?

liam.sso: i can ship a 2-line change to decode both incoming state and stored state before compare; add unit tests for duplicated encodings. target patch in next 6 hours.

ashley.cs: customer applied a fast fix: disabled query normalization for the callback path. they retried and report success: OAuth flow completed.

ashley.cs: customer notes: "We saw the redirect URL in the browser include state param that looked slightly different when captured by our edge logs vs the app log — toggling that rule fixed it." :thumbsup:

sara.support: great. next steps: 1) liam open PR for tolerant compare (link), 2) mike confirm no regressions in other providers (google) — PKCE/state handling should be provider-agnostic, 3) documentation note in support KB: "If using an edge that normalizes querystrings (Fastly/CDN), whitelist callback path from normalization rules."

liam.sso: PR opened: https://git.redwood.internal/auth/compare/issue/1489 (draft) — includes tests + changelog entry.

mike.runtime: i'll run regression matrix against google/github/cookie-sso flows.

deploy-bot: "auth-service v2.14.2 (patch) promoted to staging — includes tolerant state comparison (test-only)"

sara.support: closing loop with customer and adding CS note. marking thread resolved after patch verification. thanks everyone.

ashley.cs: resolved with customer at 11:05 UTC.
